# OBS009 `forall`

<Badge type="warning" text="warning" /> <Badge type="tip" text="enabled by default" />

A `forall` statement or construct.

## Why

`forall` is obsolescent since Fortran 2018. Its semantics (every right-hand side evaluated before
any assignment) often forces temporaries and rarely parallelises; `do concurrent` or plain array
syntax are the replacements.

## Reported

```fortran
forall (i = 1:n) a(i) = b(i) * 2
```

## Preferred

```fortran
do concurrent (i = 1:n)
  a(i) = b(i) * 2
end do
```

## Suppressing

For one occurrence, with the reason on the same line (or alone on the line before the statement):

```fortran
! fobis: ignore[OBS009] <why this occurrence is fine>
```

For the whole project, `ignore = OBS009` in the fobos [`[lint]` section](/cookbook/analysis#choose-the-rules).
